questions.question: Correct the general statement about the number of seatings: $(n-1)(n-2)/2$ is an upper bound because any chosen person has at most $\binom{n-1}{2}$ unordered pairs of neighbours. Equality is attained by the displayed construction for $n=7$, but the text does not establish attainability for every $n$.

localizations.source: Correct the general statement about the number of seatings: $(n-1)(n-2)/2$ is an upper bound because any chosen person has at most $\binom{n-1}{2}$ unordered pairs of neighbours. Equality is attained by the displayed construction for $n=7$, but the text does not establish attainability for every $n$.
localizations.ru: Исправить формулировку об общем числе рассадок: выражение $(n-1)(n-2)/2$ даёт верхнюю оценку, поскольку для любого выбранного человека существует не более $\binom{n-1}{2}$ неупорядоченных пар соседей. Равенство достигается в приведённом случае $n=7$, но из текста не следует, что оно достижимо для каждого $n$.

questions.resolution: Both editions state the general formula as an upper bound; the introduction says that fifteen breakfasts can be arranged, and the table was checked for repeated neighbour pairs.
